nodes.name: Eval CLI
nodes.responsibility: run, grade, report, check and pin, and the cancellation a person's interrupt becomes
nodes.description: Never part of the gate: every author run and the grading session call a model, and a person decides when that happens.

nodes.name: Suite loader
nodes.responsibility: Reads and validates every canonical input, refusing a fixture, a citation or a skill package that would measure the wrong thing
nodes.description: `eval:skill check` is this alone. It refuses a fixture relationship that lands on a part with children (landings.ts), a cited passage, catalogue row or rubric section the skill does not hold (citations.ts), and a skill package that names what it is graded on (leakage.ts).

nodes.name: Batch orchestrator
nodes.responsibility: Plans every arm, scenario and repetition, runs them in parallel, and can be resumed only on the same inputs
nodes.description: It hashes the inputs, the harness and both skill packages into the batch and keeps a copy of the candidate skill, so a resume or a later grading pass cannot quietly change what was measured.

nodes.name: Run isolation
nodes.responsibility: One run's private world: its own home, its own agent storage, its own CLI on the path

nodes.name: Pinned checkout
nodes.responsibility: A detached, verified checkout of one pinned Flask commit from a bare cache, or an empty repository for a planning scenario

nodes.name: Per-run server
nodes.responsibility: Starts this checkout's server on a free port against the run's own vault, and owns its shutdown

nodes.name: Skill install
nodes.responsibility: Installs through the CLI, then swaps in the arm's package, the frozen baseline or the candidate copy the batch kept, and re-derives its generated files

nodes.name: Author run
nodes.responsibility: Brings the world up, runs one author turn, and reads everything back
nodes.description: The author's stream is kept whole: its commands, its file changes, its usage and its failure are read from it afterwards, never reported by the author.

nodes.name: Guardrails
nodes.responsibility: The rules every run is held to, including whether a board file was written behind the CLI's back

nodes.name: Outcome checks
nodes.responsibility: The verdicts that need no model: what the vault, the renders and the group reports actually say

nodes.name: Captures
nodes.responsibility: Takes the picture of every board, view and variant the scenario declared, and tiles an oversize one
nodes.description: The harness takes the pictures; an author never supplies one. A declared view the author never made is a failed capture, never a default picture.

nodes.name: Grading session
nodes.responsibility: Stages a read-only workspace and grades the ungraded runs in chunks, in one resumed session of the grader chosen by name
nodes.description: The runs reach the grader blinded: an anonymous id from the batch salt, private paths redacted, and no arm anywhere in the bundle. Every run of both arms is judged against the one candidate skill the batch kept, staged beside the pinned Flask sources; a batch whose kept copy is missing or changed is refused.

nodes.name: Codex grader
nodes.responsibility: One grader runner: a resumed thread, pictures attached, usage read as the thread's running total

nodes.name: Claude grader
nodes.responsibility: The other grader runner: a resumed session, read-only tools, pictures opened from the workspace

nodes.name: Report
nodes.responsibility: Joins every run with the verdict of each grader that graded it, and says where two graders agree
nodes.description: A finding's cited passage is resolved against the kept candidate skill: one it lacks is the grader's error, one only the candidate carries is a departure the run was never shown. Written as report.md and report.json beside the batch.

nodes.name: Evaluation inputs
nodes.responsibility: The scenarios, fixtures, pins, grader settings, coverage and rubric, kept outside every skill package on purpose
nodes.description: An author reads whatever the installed skill carries. Authors that could read the scenario, the fixture and the rubric they were being measured against read them. graders.json is left out of a batch's input digest: a grader is chosen when grading runs.

nodes.name: Agent CLI
nodes.responsibility: The CLI under test, both as the author's tool and as the harness's own way of laying a fixture and reading a vault

nodes.name: Archboard server
nodes.responsibility: One per run, on its own port, against that run's vault

nodes.name: Codex CLI
nodes.responsibility: The author, and one of the two graders; pinned to an exact version a batch refuses to differ from
nodes.description: Authors run the model evals/pins.json pins (gpt-6-luna at high effort, workspace-write sandbox); the Codex grader runs the one evals/graders.json pins (gpt-6-astra at high effort, read-only).

nodes.name: Claude CLI
nodes.responsibility: The other grader, run with read-only tools and none of the operator's settings
nodes.description: claude-opus-5 at high effort with only Read, Grep and Glob, as evals/graders.json pins it.

nodes.name: CLI driver
nodes.responsibility: One call, one parsed answer: the seam every harness use of the CLI goes through

nodes.name: Skill citations
nodes.responsibility: Keeps the batch's copy of the candidate skill, and holds every cited passage, catalogue row and rubric section to a heading the skill has
nodes.description: A citation is a skill file and a heading anchor, never a line number, so rewording a passage keeps it cited and renaming a heading breaks it at check time rather than at grading.

nodes.name: Run vault
nodes.responsibility: Lays the fixture through the CLI so every id is one the product minted, and reads back the boards, renders, group reports and diagnostics

nodes.name: Command classifier
nodes.responsibility: Classes each command the author ran, and flags a read of what the run is measured against: the inputs, the harness, a skill package, another run

nodes.name: Grader retry
nodes.responsibility: Holds each answer to what the report reads, and asks once more in the same session for the runs an answer fell short on
nodes.description: Short means a declared feature left unanswered, a feature invented, or a capture offered and not observed. The retry is a call of the session like any other, so its usage counts, and it is never itself retried; a retry owed by an earlier pass is asked on the next one.

nodes.name: Exposure re-audit
nodes.responsibility: Reads each saved run's exposure again with today's classifier, so a classifier fix reaches a batch that cannot be run again

nodes.name: Comparison
nodes.responsibility: Per scenario, per workflow and for the broad case: what moved between the arms, a mean held to the noise the batch measures in itself
nodes.description: A pass count is a tally and any change to it is real; a grader mean is held to the spread of the runs the two arms share, paired scenario for scenario (report-change.ts), and gets a word only where more than one scenario stands behind it. Author and grader usage are never added together.

walkthroughs.name: How a skill change is measured

beats.heading: Two arms, everything else identical
beats.body: A batch runs the frozen baseline package and a copy of the candidate it keeps when it starts, against the same CLI, prompts, fixtures and pins, and hashes all of it into the batch. A resume on different inputs, or on a kept copy edited since, is refused rather than quietly comparing two different things.

beats.heading: Each run in a world of its own
beats.body: A run gets its own home, its own agent storage, its own checkout at a pinned commit and its own Archboard server on a free port, so nothing an author does can reach another run or the operator's machine.

beats.heading: The evidence is read from the stream, not reported
beats.body: What the author ran, what it changed and what it cost are read from its own transcript afterwards. A final board that is right proves nothing about how it got there: a board patched behind the CLI's back is a file change, and the guardrail sees it. A read of the inputs, the harness, a skill package or another run is recorded as exposure, and the report reads it again with today's classifier.

beats.heading: The harness takes the pictures
beats.body: Every board, view and variant the scenario declared is photographed by the harness and attached to the grading call. An author never supplies a picture, and a declared view nobody made is a failed capture rather than a default one.

beats.heading: The grader never learns the arm
beats.body: Runs reach the grader under anonymous ids with private paths redacted, and every run of both arms is judged against the one candidate skill the batch kept. Codex or Claude grades, chosen when grading runs; when both graded a batch, the report says where they agree rather than picking one.

beats.heading: A short answer is asked for once more
beats.body: Each verdict is held to what the report reads: every declared feature by its name, none invented, every capture observed. One that falls short is asked for again in the same session, which keeps what it read and saw; the retry costs like any call and is never itself retried.

beats.heading: What moved, held to its own noise
beats.body: The report says what moved between the arms instead of stamping a regression. A pass count is a tally and any change to it is real; a grader mean is held to the spread of the paired runs both arms share, and gets a word only where more than one scenario stands behind it.
